clue.text: Top of the pile holds good: mind what they say!

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of 'the' is used
holds means the pile word contains the next piece inside it

parts.note: a pile is a heap

explanation.surface: A warning to keep the best item at the top of a stack, and to heed the advice given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds' puts G inside HEAP after the T. London Underground announcements famously tell passengers 'Mind the gap', so the answer is the thing they say to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Underground recorded warning tells travellers to mind this space between train and platform.

clue.text: Film among the top twelve?

parts.note: something among the top is high up
twelve o'clock midday is noon

explanation.surface: Asking whether a movie made a top-twelve list.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve noon is when the clock's hands point to the top, adding to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic 1952 Western starring Gary Cooper carries this title.

clue.text: Making an impression on the way back

definitions.meaning: a remark or punch that lands with effect is said to be striking home
travelling back towards where you live

explanation.definitionFit: A blow that lands is said to go home; a returning traveller is heading home.

clue.text: Australia goes in somewhat out of practice: antidepressant needed

indicators.note: goes in means the Australia piece is placed inside the other piece
somewhat out of means only part of the word practice is taken, its opening stretch

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: the Australians are out of practice and their dressing room needs mood pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' is loose for taking just the first four letters, and 'goes in' places the Australia piece inside them; the surface is a cricket team rusty before a Test.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand name of fluoxetine, a widely prescribed antidepressant drug.

clue.text: See who it is and take his side?

definitions.meaning: to recognise and name a person
to sympathise with someone, as in feeling at one with them

explanation.definitionFit: To recognise who someone is, and to identify with a person is to share their viewpoint.

clue.text: In the unlikely event that I cool it in 60% of handicap with 75% present

parts.note: to cool something by blowing air is to fan it

indicators.note: in means the it piece sits inside the shortened handicap word
60% of a ten-letter word keeps its first six letters

parts.note: a handicap is a disability
taken as written

indicators.note: 75% of a four-letter word keeps its first three letters

parts.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone telling themselves to calm down while handicapped, with three-quarters of the field present.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' keeps DISABI, the first six of ten letters, and 'in' puts the it inside that; '75%' keeps three of four letters. The phrase is said of a condition unlikely to be met.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom stresses that a condition is very unlikely to be met, hence a remote eventuality.

clue.text: I met chap suffering with stress

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are in a bad way, battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a man who was in distress and under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking emphatically means putting strong stress or force on the words.

clue.text: Multiplied by triple or quadruple, say

definitions.meaning: the arithmetic word for multiplication, as in three by four
three-fold and four-fold are examples of so many multiples

explanation.definitionFit: Multiplication is read as 'times', and three times or four times describe a triple or quadruple.

clue.text: Destined to keep German city in association with 15?

indicators.note: to keep means the destined word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: destined means fated
Ulm is a city in southern Germany, birthplace of Einstein
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fate keeps a German city in some partnership with another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'association with' links to the cross-reference: the answer is in association with, i.e. akin to, the answer at 15 (THUNDERED).
explanation.definitionFit: Latin fulminare means to hurl lightning or to thunder, so the two verbs are near synonyms.

clue.text: Roman farmer with a lot of money in Madrid in silver and note

indicators.note: in means the Spanish word sits inside the silver-plus-note pair

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
la is a note of the sol-fa scale

parts.words: with a lot of money in Madrid
parts.note: in Madrid, Spanish for wealthy is rico

explanation.surface: A wealthy Roman agriculturalist living in Madrid, dealing in silver and banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Agricola is Latin for farmer and was also the name of a Roman general, Tacitus's father-in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for one who tills the fields, and the name of a famous Roman governor of Britain.

clue.text: Spot politician in big money

indicators.note: in means the politician is placed inside the big money

parts.note: a pile is a large fortune
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a politician among great wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small spot or blemish on the skin.

clue.text: Responsibility toward paper craft

parts.note: the Guardian is a British national newspaper
a ship is a sea craft

explanation.surface: A newspaper's attitude to producing quality work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a legal guardian means having charge of and duty of care for someone.

clue.text: Spin number with stake holding single currency in Africa

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

indicators.note: holding means the stake word contains the next pieces

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
the pula is the currency of Botswana

explanation.surface: A spin doctor betting on the euro being adopted in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin facts is to present them deviously, to control or twist them.

clue.text: Sculptor, one that employs wassailer

parts.note: Sir Anthony Caro was a British abstract sculptor
one who uses something is a user

explanation.definitionFit: To wassail is to drink and make merry, as a carouser does.

clue.text: If bu is bus, ___ (or train) (early English hero)

parts.note: by analogy with 'bu' for bus, the blank is a two-letter start of the next vehicle
taken as written
a tram is a street train

explanation.surface: A nonsense analogy puzzle about vehicles and their abbreviations, solved by a medieval knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Just as 'bu' stands for bus, 'tr' stands for tram (or train): fill the blank as 'TR is TRAM'. Tristram is the Tristan of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tristram, the Cornish knight of the Round Table, is a hero of early English romance.

clue.text: Edoverth!

parts.note: the letters ED sit over the letters TH, so TH lies beneath ED

explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition here; the cross-reference at 8 supplies it as a near synonym of FULMINATED.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture is the whole clue: letters stacked so that one pair lies beneath the other, which spoken as a phrase gives a verb for roaring loudly.

clue.text: King of England, not Germany, and part of Scotland, not at home

indicators.note: not means the letter for Germany is removed

parts.note: Alfred the Great was a king of the English
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: part of means only the opening stretch of the word Scotland is used

explanation.surface: A list of British territories, with the king out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: In Italian al fresco means 'in the fresh air', so outdoors rather than indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining outdoors rather than inside the house is eating in the open air.

clue.text: Be charitable to soldier with meat at hand

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
veal is calf meat
MS, manuscript, is something written by hand

explanation.surface: Feed a soldier with meat that is readily available as an act of charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food to the poor, so giving them is a charitable act.

clue.text: See 13
Archer's flutter

definitions.meaning: an archer's possession: the case holding his arrows

explanation.definitionFit: An arrow case carried by an archer, and also a trembling or shiver.

clue.text: Would-be adventurers not 3?

definitions.meaning: the name of an organisation running outdoor adventure courses
heading away from home rather than returning towards it

explanation.definitionFit: Outward Bound runs outdoor challenge courses, and ships heading out are opposite to those returning.

clue.text: Prophet's host gives bard's friend a drink

parts.note: Mr W.H. is the dedicatee of Shakespeare's sonnets
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A host gives Shakespeare's companion something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophet is Jonah, who spent three days inside a great fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonah was swallowed by a great sea creature which thus played host to him.

clue.text: See 2
Persecute artists in holds

indicators.note: in means the artists go inside the holds word

parts.note: holds means has
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Artists persecuted while trapped in ships' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to pester and persecute persistently.

clue.text: Leading Conservative service or boss?

parts.note: Michael Gove was a leading Conservative politician
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Tory grandee in the navy is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Governor is informal British slang ('guv') for a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the governor is the person in charge, one's employer.

clue.text: Partners' bloom reversed by mutant

parts.note: W and E are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: reversed means the bloom word is written backwards

parts.note: a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: A couple's flower turned upside down by a genetic freak.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who changes into a wolf is a kind of shapeshifting mutant.

clue.text: Animal at home among rubbish

indicators.note: among means the home goes inside the rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a den is an animal's home

explanation.surface: An animal found at its home among piles of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat or mouse is a rodent, a kind of gnawing animal.
